parts.label: main
parts.technique: constant acceleration kinematics in vector form
parts.reason: M7.3 explicitly covers constant acceleration formulae extended to 2 dimensions using vectors, and finding speed from a velocity vector uses magnitude (P10.2).

parts.label: a
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers graphs in kinematics including velocity-time graphs for motion under constant acceleration (up and down).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat / area under v-t graph for max height
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae; M7.2 covers area under v-t graph interpretation as displacement.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: conservation of linear momentum in a collision
parts.reason: No statement in M6-M9 mentions momentum, impulse or collisions; this concept is entirely absent from the given specification statements, so it is out.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: reasoning about direction of motion after collision using momentum result
parts.reason: Depends on the momentum result from part (a), which is out of spec (no momentum/collision statement exists).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: impulse calculation from change in momentum
parts.reason: Impulse is not mentioned in any M6-M9 statement, and this part also depends on the out-of-spec momentum equation from (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: moments equilibrium of a rigid rod (bench) with multiple point loads
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers moments in simple static contexts including problems involving parallel coplanar forces on a rigid body.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: moments equilibrium with unknown position and reaction ratio
parts.reason: Same moments technique as (a), still simple static equilibrium of a rod under parallel forces, covered by M9.1.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: drawing forces on a particle on a rough inclined plane (weight, normal reaction, friction, applied force)
parts.reason: M8.6 covers friction on rough surfaces; M8.1 covers forces including normal reaction; M8.2 guidance covers particle on inclined plane.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.technique: resolving forces perpendicular to incline with friction to find normal reaction, on point of slipping
parts.reason: M8.6 covers F ≤ μR model and limiting friction/statics; M8.2 guidance covers resolving forces on inclined plane.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.technique: resolving forces parallel to incline to find applied force P using limiting friction
parts.reason: Same as above, resolving forces with friction on inclined plane, covered by M8.6/M8.2 guidance.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: finding angle of resultant vector force with j direction
parts.reason: M8.5 covers addition and resultant of forces, and finding direction of a vector relates to P10.2 (magnitude/direction form); this is a standard resultant force direction calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: algebraic manipulation of resultant force components parallel to given vector
parts.reason: M8.5 covers resultant forces given in component form; deriving a relation from parallel vectors is standard vector/force work covered by M8.5 and P10.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law with resultant force vector to find mass from acceleration magnitude
parts.reason: M8.2 covers Newton's second law for forces given as 2-D vectors, and magnitude of vector links to P10.2.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: connected particles via string over pulley on inclined plane, Newton's second law, simultaneous equations for acceleration and tension
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly covers problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles where forces need to be resolved, at least one particle on an inclined plane.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law applied to one block in contact with another to find contact force
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly mentions connected particle problems including particles in contact (e.g. lift problems), which matches Q on R.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: resultant of two tension forces acting on a pulley using resolved components/trigonometry
parts.reason: M8.5 covers addition of forces and resultant forces including resolving into components or using a vector diagram for two or more forces given in magnitude-direction form.
